findings.where: Screen 12, A screw is a ramp (and lesson sources)
findings.what: The screw claims (a thread is a ramp wrapped round a shaft, and the advantage is circumference ÷ pitch) have no entry in the lesson's sources and no K.check; research-notes.md already holds the BoxSand and TeachEngineering quotes, so add one as source 5 with a check.

findings.where: Screen 3, Counting ways to move, text
findings.what: The text goes from "each joint can move two ways" straight to "Three of those ways slide or turn the whole frame", so it skips the 2j total and "those" reads as one joint's two ways; add "So j joints have 2j ways to move." before it, as the explanation does.

The puzzle is set at the left foot, the pin that screen 6 says "can push any way", but the Why never says the pin pushes nothing sideways here because no other force on the frame pushes sideways; add that sentence or set the puzzle at the roller foot.
"Each bar stops one of the rest" is stated as always true, and screen 13 then shows a bar that stops nothing, so write "Each bar can stop one of the rest".

It asks for the 5 bars that screen 3's counter and words showed one screen earlier ("needs 2 × 4 − 3 = 5"), which tests memory rather than the rule; use a frame screen 3 did not count, such as five joints needing 7 bars.
"Start at a joint with only two unknown bars" never says why two; add one sentence saying a joint's balance gives two equations, across and up, so it can find two unknowns.

findings.where: Screen 12 and the lesson as a whole
findings.what: The screw is a SHOW screen with no DO puzzle, and the brief's links for it are missing (a finer thread gives more advantage, a loose screw terminal runs hot), as is the lifting-beam and spreader-beam example, so the screw connects to neither the frames nor Dan's trade.
Drawn to true scale, a 2 mm climb over 62.8 mm is an almost flat line, so the unrolled thread barely reads as a ramp; draw the climb taller and label it as drawn taller.
"The load lifted is bigger than the push by the ramp's length ÷ its climb" reads as adding an amount, not multiplying; write "push × 62.8 mm = load × 2 mm, so the load is 31.4 times the push".
"Hang the load on a joint." does not say how to do it; write "Tap a joint to hang the load there."

The breaks miss that node balances alone rarely settle a circuit's branch currents (Ohm's law or loop equations are also needed), while a simple frame's joint balances alone give every bar force; Dan, as an electrician, will notice.

There are four footnotes, and two of them sit on things Dan would not look up ([^2] a triangle is rigid, [^3] the moment balance he already knows); keep [^1] (m = 2j − 3) and [^4] (tension and compression at the pin).
Its second sentence chains three clauses in 25 words ("Under a load, each bar is pulled or pushed..., and balancing... tells you which, and how hard"); split it into two short sentences.
The four-line lead at 360 px pushes every task down the screen and talks about frames even on the screw screen; shorten it to one line.
